name: 4.0 Flat-Six NA
notes: Variant: Porsche 911 GT3 (992.2, model year 2025 on; Porsche technical data '911 GT3 (PDK)', MY S 10/2024, EU model) with the standard seven-speed PDK (3.75/2.38/1.72/1.34/1.11/0.96/0.84) and the 4.54 rear-axle ratio, rear-wheel drive, on the standard rear 315/30 ZR 21 tyre (driven axle; front 255/35 ZR 20). Overall ratio = gear x 4.54 (Porsche lists no other fixed stage). The optional six-speed GT manual and the Touring Package are not modelled. Engine: 3,996 cc (102.0 x 81.5 mm) naturally aspirated flat-six (boxer), 375 kW (510 PS) at 8,500 rpm, 450 Nm at 6,250 rpm (the 2025 US press kit gives 502 hp and 331 lb-ft), maximum engine speed 9,000 rpm, which is also the US press kit's '9,000 rpm redline'. Combustion entries are listed in firing order 1-6-2-4-3-5 at the even 720/6 = 120 deg interval. Porsche numbers cylinders 1-3 on one bank and 4-6 on the other, so bank 0 = cylinders 1-3 and bank 1 = cylinders 4-6, and the banks strictly alternate (bank 0 at 0/240/480, bank 1 at 120/360/600). Which physical side is bank 0 is not needed for angle/bank data. Source caveat: the firing order is printed in Porsche's 911 Carrera (996) workshop manual (water-cooled M96 flat-six, 1997 and MY2002 pages); no public Porsche document seen states it for the 992 GT3 engine itself, so the Porsche flat-six order is assumed unchanged. The 1-3 / 4-6 bank grouping is confirmed by Porsche for the 991 GT3 (Technical Information 59/15: per-bank camshafts 'Cylinders 1-3' / 'Cylinders 4-6') and for the 4.0 GT3 Cup (991 II) engine ('Lambda cyl. 1-3/4-6'). EPA: every 911 GT3 row in the EPA Test Car Lists is the 992.1 predecessor (MY2022-2024): PDK axle 4.19, N/V 43.0 (the MY2022-2023 PDK rows give 8 gears, a data-entry quirk for the 7-speed PDK; MY2024 lists 7), and manual axle 3.76 (N/V 40.3, MY2022-2023) or 3.96 (N/V 43.0, MY2024). The MY2025 and MY2026 lists (versions of 2026-01-21) have no 911 GT3 row. EPA rows are for the 992.1 (axle 4.19 PDK / 3.96 manual); no N/V row. Consistency checks (not automated): Porsche's US press kit states that the 992.2 final drive is 'eight percent shorter than in the predecessor', and Porsche's 992.1 PDK sheet (02/2021) lists the same seven gear ratios with a 4.19 final drive (4.54 / 4.19 = 1.084). Scaling the EPA 992.1 N/V 43.0 by 1.084 gives 46.6 rpm/mph, against 46.47 from this model (-0.3 %). The model also puts 9,000 rpm in 7th at 311.7 km/h (193.7 mph), matching Porsche's 311 km/h (US: 193 mph) top speed, which is therefore reached at the rev limit. Generation differences, not conflicts: the 992.1 made 375 kW at 8,400 rpm and 470 Nm at 6,100 rpm with a 318 km/h top speed. Estimated (not published in the sources used): idle 800 rpm; limiter type fuel-hard at the published 9,000 rpm maximum with 150 rpm hysteresis (Porsche documents rev limitation 'by fuel cutoff and E-gas' for the 996 flat-six; hard vs soft and the hysteresis are estimates); shiftTimeS 0.10 s (PDK type default; Porsche gives no shift-time figure).
